glm.feedback:
Findings:

- Category: bug
  Severity: low
  File: client/src/lib/sessionInfoFormat.ts:7-16 (`formatTokens`)
  Finding: `999_999` formats as `"1000k"` instead of `"1M"` (the `k >= 100` branch rounds to 1000 before the millions branch is ever reached). Any token count in [999_950, 999_999] displays a nonsensical "1000k".
  Suggestion: After computing the rounded kilovalue, if it is ≥ 1000 fall through to the millions branch (or format from the original number).

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: medium
  File: client/src/components/external/mission/MissionInfoPanel.tsx:44-46
  Finding: `useProject(unassigned ? "" : task.projectId)` — when the task is unassigned the hook is called with an empty string. If `useProject` does not internally guard falsy ids (not visible in the diff), this fires a request to `/projects/` (or `/projects/%20`-style URL) on every unassigned mount. Even if guarded, the intent is unclear and fragile.
  Suggestion: Confirm `useProject("")` is a no-op; if not, skip the call (e.g. return `data: undefined` for empty id) or make the id optional and null-safe.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: client/src/hooks/useSessionInfo.ts:40-49
  Finding: The task-state-change refetch effect swallows transitions that happen while the panel is inactive (`taskId` null): `lastState.current` is updated on every render, so if the state changes while hidden, the change is consumed with no fetch; on re-activation the data can be up to `staleTime` (30 s) old with no compensating refetch trigger beyond mount-staleness.
  Suggestion: Only advance `lastState.current` when a refetch actually fires (or reset `lastState` when `taskId` goes from null to a value).

- Category: bug
  Severity: low
  File: client/src/components/external/mission/MissionInfoSidebar.tsx:124
  Finding: `active={visible && !(!compact && layout.collapsed)}` — the second clause is dead code: when `!compact && layout.collapsed` the component already returned the rail button at line ~52, so `MissionInfoPanel` can never render in that state. Harmless but misleading; the real intent (desktop CSS-yield when an artifact is open below 1700px) is NOT covered — the panel keeps its query active and keeps refetching on window focus while visually `display:none` behind `:has(.artifact)`.
  Suggestion: Drop the dead clause; if the artifact-open yield should also pause scanning, that requires signal from MissionBody (e.g. a prop) rather than the unreachable expression.

- Category: bug
  Severity: medium
  File: client/src/components/external/mission/MissionInfoSidebar.tsx:31-33, 63-68
  Finding: Unassigned-task segment handling: `const seg = unassigned ? "info" : layout.segment;` — if the persisted/global state is `viewer`/`folders` and the user switches to an unassigned task, the segmented control renders with value `info` while `layout.segment` stays `viewer`. Any code that reads `layout.segment` (or a future `onChange`) is now inconsistent with what's displayed; also `mission-side-body-${seg}` testid uses the forced value, so state and DOM can diverge. Additionally `open()` calls `layout.setSegment("viewer")` unconditionally — for an unassigned task, clicking an output (they're inert, so currently unreachable) or any future path would persist a segment that cannot render.
  Suggestion: Normalize once: on mount / when `unassigned` becomes true, `setSegment("info")`, and derive everything from `layout.segment`.

- Category: test
  Severity: low
  File: client/src/components/external/mission/MissionInfoSidebar.test.tsx:118-120 ("no session yet")
  Finding: The mock is set with `mockImplementation` in `beforeEach`'s `fetchMock` already assigned, then re-assigned inside the test after `mount()`? No — it's re-assigned before `mount()`, fine. However the "Refresh recovers" test (line ~127) uses `mockImplementationOnce` for the failure but react-query `retry: false` is per-QueryClient default here — that is set. Real gap: no test covers a **malformed/200-with-garbage** response or `info.context.tokens === null` with status ok ("No usage recorded yet" branch of `env-context-empty` is never exercised), and `env-outputs-empty` is untested.
  Suggestion: Add a case with `status:"ok"` and `tokens: null` / empty `outputs` to pin the "No usage/files recorded yet" copy, which a broken implementation would otherwise render as "Loading…" forever or crash on.

- Category: regression
  Severity: low
  File: client/src/components/external/mission/MissionCompactTabs.tsx:33-40, 69-73
  Finding: The roving-tabindex handler and `internalRefs` indexing are not shown updated for the new 4th tab; the diff only patches the ref callback (`if (refs[tab.id])`) and the TABS list. If `handleKeyDown` uses `enabled.indexOf` vs `internalRefs` indexed over the full TABS array (the ref callback writes `internalRefs.current[index]` where `index` is the full-list index), ArrowLeft/Right navigation can land on a null slot for a disabled Detail tab — the previous 3-column layout coincidentally aligned; nothing in the diff proves the 4-tab mapping is correct. The e2e/unit tests never exercise keyboard navigation between tabs.
  Suggestion: Verify/adjust the index arithmetic in `handleKeyDown` for the 4-tab case and add a keyboard-nav test.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: client/src/lib/sessionInfoFormat.ts:24-27
  Finding: Comment says case-insensitive prefix match applies "only for drive-letter (Windows) paths", but the implementation compares the entire prefix case-insensitively for any `cwd` starting with a drive letter — meaning `C:\Dev\App\...` vs project `c:/dev/app` matches, but `D:\Foo` vs `d:/foo` also matches, and the drive-detection is keyed on the *cwd*, so a UNC path (`\\server\share`) cwd with a drive-letter output (or vice versa) is silently rejected or compared case-sensitively against expectations. Behavior is safe (rejects), just diverges from the documented contract.
  Suggestion: Either tighten to compare only the drive prefix case-insensitively, or fix the comment; add a UNC test case.

- Category: test
  Severity: low
  File: client/e2e/flows/M3-mission-info-sidebar.spec.ts:96-99
  Finding: The "no timer" assertion waits 3.5 s of idle and expects zero new requests, but the hook has `refetchOnWindowFocus: true` — in CI a focus event (e.g. between steps) would add a hit and flake the test; conversely the assertion doesn't distinguish "no timer" from "no focus refetch". Also `refetchOnWindowFocus` itself is untested behavior that could regress to a polling loop without any test noticing at longer intervals.
  Suggestion: Assert against `SESSION_INFO_STALE_MS` window semantics explicitly or disable focus refetch in the test page to make the "no timer" claim deterministic.

Spec compliance overall is good: segments, resizable/remembered sidebar, FolderTree reuse, compact Info tab entry, mission-*/env-* testids, no textarea, no percentage, session-info consumption, motion-token note (static CSS). No security issues found — path relativization defensively rejects traversal and the Viewer stays project-scoped.

Overall: solid implementation with correct structure and genuinely behavior-pinning tests; the findings are localized fixes (segment-state divergence on unassigned tasks, formatTokens 1000k, possibly useProject("") firing) worth addressing before ship.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
